subject: Near-green suite residue: 8 rows across op/args, context, crypt, delete, or — triaged to rows, not yet diagnosed
description:
DONE s319 — all 8 rows probed and dispositioned.  Nothing left unclassified.

REGISTERED as expected divergences (each is its file's ONLY failing row, so the
all-or-nothing bar is met; both probe-confirmed, not description-matched):
  op/args.t  t23 -> XDIFF, §DESTROY called by garbage collector.  PCL agrees on
      t21/t22 (flag stays 0 in f and after f) and misses only the scope-exit
      DESTROY.  Verified XDIFF in the runner.
  op/crypt.t t6  -> XDIFF, §Unicode semantics differences.  PCL's crypt VALUE is
      correct (t5 passes); only utf8::is_utf8 differs — no per-scalar UTF-8
      flag.  Verified XDIFF in the runner.

REAL BUGS, each with its own task (all three files correctly stay UNEXPLAINED):
  op/delete.t t26/t54 -> task #163.  delete is NOT the bug: \$h{k} != \$h{k}
      already, before delete is involved.  Ref identity keys on the WRAPPER box
      p-backslash allocates, not on the referent.  Needs the §1 data-model
      ruling — flagged in review-requests §9.  (t56 is DESTROY-via-GC, a
      different blessed gap, which is why the FILE cannot be registered.)
  op/context.t t8 -> task #164.  A trailing `BEGIN { }` steals the sub's tail
      position, so the preceding statement gets VOID instead of scalar.  A/B
      probe: identical sub WITHOUT the BEGIN is correct.  Fix = skip
      compile-time-only blocks when finding a block's tail statement.
  op/or.t t9/t10 -> task #165.  `||` does not propagate lvalue context to its
      operands, so the foreach alias binds a copy.  Constraint: sibling rows
      t11/t12 assert || must NOT propagate to a SUBSCRIPT (no autoviv), so a
      blanket fix breaks them.

METHOD WORTH REUSING for the rest of #150's near-green list: one run-perl-suite
pass over several small files with --faillog yields every diverging row with
perl's own description; then probe each row A/B (with and without the suspected
trigger) before believing the description.  Two of these eight rows blamed the
wrong feature entirely (delete, and "crypt" which is really the utf8 flag).
